explained.tdh.sure.meta.title: How sure: what is proved about TDH | 6529 Explained
explained.tdh.sure.meta.description: What is proved about the TDH rules, what is tested every day, and what is not, read from the Lean manifest.
explained.tdh.sure.title: What is proved, what is tested, and what is not.
explained.tdh.sure.lede: Lean, a proof assistant, checks every step of a proof: the proofs show that a Lean model of the rules has the properties it states, and the daily check shows that one day followed the rules.
explained.tdh.sure.drift: These proofs are about the rules under their old name, {oldName}, as the manifest written {written} records. D136 (four wallets) and D137 (the name TDH v1.4) came after it; the counts below are that manifest's.
explained.tdh.sure.moved.label: A newer model
explained.tdh.sure.moved.body: 6529's design record has the Lean model at {leanCommit} ({leanDay}); this manifest was built from {commit}. The counts and statements here are the manifest's until the feed serves the new one.

explained.tdh.sure.src.vectors: P26 vectors {passed} of {total} in this manifest
explained.tdh.sure.layers.label: Two questions
explained.tdh.sure.layers.title: Is the rule what it claims? Did the day follow it?
explained.tdh.sure.layers.body: Lean answers the first, for the properties it states; the daily check answers the second, one day at a time. A proof says nothing about a day's inputs, and a green day nothing about the rule's properties.
explained.tdh.sure.rule.vectorsDetail: Inputs with their exact expected outputs.
explained.tdh.sure.rule.provedDetail: {count} claims, each with what it does not cover.
explained.tdh.sure.rule.programsDetail: No proof links any program's code to the model.
explained.tdh.sure.day.recomputedDetail: Two separately written programs, equal to 6529.io.
explained.tdh.sure.day.zkDetail: Proof A states cycle {cycle}'s roots and a total of {total}, without the burn addresses, under the retired {version} rules; mainnet's SP1 verifier accepts it in a read-only call. Checking its anchor block against Ethereum is the contract's step. {link}
explained.tdh.sure.day.recordedDetail: The contract would accept a day only with both proofs.
explained.tdh.sure.featured.label: One claim, to the end
explained.tdh.sure.featured.title: Refuted twice in one day, then narrowed to what is proved.
explained.tdh.sure.featured.body: On {day}, P26 gained a sentence saying that steps inside one transaction cannot change TDH. The Lean model showed it false within hours, then showed a narrower version false too. The sentence that stands is the one the proof covers: such steps change no holding stack.
explained.tdh.sure.part.first.quote: “inserting, removing or reordering steps that leave every {net} unchanged changes no value”
explained.tdh.sure.part.narrowed.quote: “…changes no stack, balance or raw (… proved in the Lean model)”
explained.tdh.sure.part.first.body: Insert a mint and a burn of {copies} copies of one card into a transaction. Every net movement is unchanged, but the card's minted count rises from {mintedBefore} to {mintedAfter}, so H doubles, another card's rate goes from {rateBefore} to {rateAfter} and B's TDH from {finalBefore} to {finalAfter}.
explained.tdh.sure.part.first.cap: Checked by evaluation, which trusts Lean's compiler, on an example registry.
explained.tdh.sure.part.narrowed.body: The proof covered the stacks only. A mint and its burn can move a card's first mint earlier, make it eligible and give a wallet a balance it did not have. H rises from {hBefore} to {hAfter}, and B's TDH from {finalBefore} to {finalAfter}.
explained.tdh.sure.part.narrowed.cap: Checked by evaluation. Here P26 had cited the proof for more than it proved.
explained.tdh.sure.part.proved.notCovere: two cycle inputs. It holds for two canonical sequences whose transactions correspond one to one and in order, when both replays have a result.
explained.tdh.sure.sketch.summary: How the proof goes, in four theorems
explained.tdh.sure.sketch.intro: Each step is a theorem in the manifest, checked in Lean's kernel. Read in order, they are the argument.
explained.tdh.sure.sketch.pairs: a transaction's netted pairs depend only on each address's net change, so two transactions with the same net changes give the same pairs.
explained.tdh.sure.sketch.one: two transactions with one timestamp and one hash, in which every address has the same net movement of every token, leave every stack the same.
explained.tdh.sure.sketch.all: taking two inputs one transaction at a time, the whole replay depends only on each transaction's net movements, when their transactions correspond one to one and in order.
explained.tdh.sure.sketch.cycle: the same holds for a whole cycle's canonical sequences of transfers, whenever both replays have a result. This is the claim.
explained.tdh.sure.sketch.close: What the chain does not reach: the canonical sort before the replay, and anything beyond the stacks, such as a card's minted count (cases H and I).
explained.tdh.sure.claims.label: The claims
explained.tdh.sure.claims.title: Each claim, with its limit beside it.
explained.tdh.sure.claims.falseByKind: The {count} statements shown false, by kind: {firstRule} against the first netting rule, replaced on {day} after program B found the flaw; {netting} that narrowed the netting sentence ({nettingCases}); {never} properties the rules never had ({neverCases}); and {p53} about validator rules.
explained.tdh.sure.claims.capDrift: D148 exempts the network’s two accounts from the {cap} cap, and D150 makes them two separate parties, each counting toward the six-party rule. The claim above, like the Lean model, caps every party.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.1.detail: Two replays whose transactions match one to one, in order, with the same net movements, leave every holding stack the same, whenever both have a result.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.1.limit: From two sorted sequences, not two days' raw inputs: no theorem goes through the canonical sort. Not for values beyond the stacks (cases H and I).
explained.tdh.sure.claim.2.detail: A stack's size is its balance, and balances never go negative.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.2.limit: “Held = minted − burned” is false when a burn address sends; held = copies from burn addresses − copies to them (case G).
explained.tdh.sure.claim.3.detail: An identity's balance, raw and base TDH are the sums over its wallets.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.3.limit: Not final TDH, since one boost covers the identity: two wallets with one Gradient each have finals of {wallet} + {wallet}, but together they hold two Gradients and a bigger boost, so the identity's is {identity} (case F). The day's total is the sum of identities by definition.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.4.detail: Any order of the same inputs gives the same result, for decoded inputs and raw logs.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.4.limit: The header and claims maps are taken as fixed; which bad log an error names can depend on order.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.5a.detail: No validator party exceeds {cap} of the registered weight, within six passes.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.5a.limit: Needs six or more parties of positive weight, and keys kept valid. The bound is on the registered weight: on a day when some of it does not sign, a party's share of what signed can be larger.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.5b.detail: No evidence shortens a validator's exclusion in force, for a node that keeps incident records.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.5b.limit: False for a node that recomputes incidents from the evidence it still holds.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.6.detail: The model on decoded inputs is the model on raw logs; a day with a result has every value at its type.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.6.limit: The input rules are definitions, checked by vectors, not theorems.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.7.detail: No group exceeds the registry's limit, every two of its wallets are linked, and a fourth joins only through the fresh-link gate.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.7.limit: Which possible group the newest-first order picks is pinned by vectors, not proved; so is the match with 6529.io's code.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.stack.detail: The model's stack behaves as P26 §7.1's ordered list.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.stack.limit: How a stack is stored, not what the replay puts in it, which the first two claims cover.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.other.detail: A section of the manifest this page does not describe yet.
explained.tdh.sure.claim.other.limit: See its entries under Every statement.
explained.tdh.sure.not.label: What you still have to trust
explained.tdh.sure.not.title: A proof moves trust; it does not remove it.
explained.tdh.sure.ledger.kernel: Lean's kernel and its three standard axioms are sound
explained.tdh.sure.ledger.kernelCovers: The base every proof rests on. It cannot be proved in Lean.
explained.tdh.sure.ledger.model: The model says what P26 says
explained.tdh.sure.ledger.modelCovers: The vectors on every change; the day of {day} replayed record by record, and {random} random inputs against the Python reference, each run once; and review.
explained.tdh.sure.ledger.programs: The programs compute what the model computes
explained.tdh.sure.ledger.programsCovers: The vectors, and one day replayed through the model once. The daily check compares the programs with each other and with 6529.io, never with the model.
explained.tdh.sure.ledger.rerunCovers: The model's source is private. The manifest names its commit, {commit}, a commitment to the source that will be published with it.
explained.tdh.sure.limits.label: The {count} limits
explained.tdh.sure.limit.1.canonical-sor: No theorem goes from a day's input through the canonical sort to the replay.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.1.balance-raw-s: If a card's eligibility stays the same, its balance and raw stay the same too. That follows from the definitions; it is not a theorem.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.3.identity-wall: The identity record's own wallets field is not proved to be its wallet list.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.4.maps-fixed: The header and claims maps are taken as fixed.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.4.error-names: Which malformed log an error names can depend on input order.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.5a.inputs-taken: Each account's keys after the no-pool rule, and the lease, are inputs, not proved.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.5b.not-covered: Joining nodes, nodes' differing views and fault attribution are not covered.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.6.rules-are-def: The input rules are definitions, checked by P26's vectors.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.6.json-reader: The vector runner's JSON reader is test tooling, not proved.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.7.greedy-order: Which possible group the newest-first order picks is pinned by vectors, not proved.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.7.pair-key-orde: The pair key's text order is checked on examples, not proved.
explained.tdh.sure.limit.7.backend-code: No theorem relates the model to 6529.io's own code; vectors and the references test it.
explained.tdh.sure.theorems.label: In words and in Lean
explained.tdh.sure.theorems.title: Each claim's main theorem, as Lean states it.
explained.tdh.sure.theorems.body: Pick a claim to read its main theorem in words and in Lean, from the model at {commit}, proof left out. The last line is the claim; the lines above it, what it assumes.
explained.tdh.sure.theorems.name: Lean name
explained.tdh.sure.theorems.noLean: The Lean text is not shown: the copy kept with this page is from another commit than the manifest's.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.1.replayHoldi: Replay two lists of transfers whose transactions match one to one and in order, each pair with the same net movement for every wallet: every wallet ends with the same stack of copies, whenever both replays have a result.
The last line is the claim: for every token k and wallet w, the two stacks are equal. Above it, the assumptions: hg, the transactions correspond; hr₁ and hr₂, both replays have a result.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.2.replay_ok.w: Once the underflow test passes, the replay succeeds, and no debit ever finds too few copies: every wallet's stack holds exactly its balance, what it received minus what it sent. That is “balances are never negative”, and why P26 need not test it again.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.2.replay_ok.r: hU is the passed underflow test. The claim after ∃ h: the replay gives holdings h, and for every token k and every wallet w outside the burn addresses, the stack's size is the balance.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.3.computeCycl: In every day's result, an identity's balance, raw days and base TDH, in total and card by card, are the sums of the same values over exactly its wallets, each counted once.

h: the day has a result. For each identity record ri there is a list of wallets ms with no repeats (Nodup), exactly the wallets with that identity's key, and ri's balance, raw and base are sums over their records rws. The last line: every wallet has its identity's record.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.4.computeCycl: Shuffle a day's transfers, its consolidation events and its ignored logs in any way: the result is the same, or the same error.
ts, es and is are any reorderings (Perm) of the three lists. The claim: computing the cycle with them equals computing it with the originals.
With six or more parties of positive weight, no validator party, capped or not, counts for more than {cap} of the counted total, which is the registered weight.
{six}: at least six parties. The claim: for every party p, its counted weight is at most {cap} of the counted total, written in whole numbers so that nothing rounds.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.5b.steps_keep: No evidence, in any order or number, ever removes a cycle from a validator's exclusion: an exclusion in force is never shortened.
h: cycle c is excluded under the incidents incs. The claim: after any list of faults fs, taken one step at a time (foldl step), c is still excluded.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.6.computeCycl: Given no raw logs, the model on raw logs computes exactly the model on decoded inputs. So every theorem about the decoded model also holds for the raw one, in the case where every log comes decoded.
hl: no raw logs; hh: every header's block and time fits its type. The claim: computing from the source equals checking the registry (p.check), then computing the cycle from its decoded items.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.7.computeCycl: In every day's result, no identity holds more wallets than the registry allows, every two of its wallets are linked both ways, and a group larger than {ungated} has one wallet whose links with all the others are fresh: D136's gate.

h: the day has a result. Every cluster c has no repeats (Nodup), at most consolidationMaxWallets wallets, a confirmed link between any two (ConfirmedLink), and, when larger than the ungated size, a member m with a fresh link (FreshLink) to every other.
explained.tdh.sure.theorem.stack.takeLas: Taking n copies from a stack takes the last n, in order, and the rest of the stack followed by them is the stack as it was: the model's stack behaves as P26 §7.1's list.
h: takeLast succeeds, giving moved and rest. The claim: rest followed by the moved copies, expanded, is the original stack, and exactly n copies moved.
explained.tdh.sure.build.label: How Lean checks it
explained.tdh.sure.build.title: Every proof is checked again at every build.
explained.tdh.sure.build.body: A proof is a term Lean's kernel checks; a wrong or missing one fails the build. What one build established, as its manifest records:
explained.tdh.sure.build.kernelBody: {command} compiles the model with Lean {version}, in {jobs} jobs, and checks every proof in the kernel.
explained.tdh.sure.build.auditBody: An audit checks that each of the {count} named theorems rests on {axioms} and nothing else. A {sorry} fails it, and so does {native}, which trusts the compiler.
explained.tdh.sure.build.falseBody: {kernel} are theorems the kernel checks, by {decide}. The other {evaluation} run the model on an example ({guard}), as do the {facts} checks of P26's stated facts: those trust Lean's compiler.
explained.tdh.sure.build.falseRef: in the kernel or by evaluation
explained.tdh.sure.build.vectorsBody: {passed} of {total} pass ({checks} checks); {reasons} of {total} again with every rejection citing its section; and the model's own netting vectors, {nettingPassed} of {nettingTotal}.
explained.tdh.sure.build.ciBody: 6529's design record reruns it all, with both references, on every change to the model or P26, and fails if the committed manifest differs from the tree's.
